title: Potsdam to host new Europa Nostra Heritage Hub with a focus on climate resilience, civic engagement and youth capacity-building
content:
The State Capital City of Potsdam has entered into a strategic partnership with Europa Nostra, the leading European heritage civil society organisation. On 29 October 2026, a Memorandum of Understanding for the establishment the Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Potsdam was signed at the Old Town Hall by Potsdam’s Lord Mayor Noosha Aubel, the Secretary-General of Europa Nostra, Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović, and the President of Europa Nostra Germany, Dr. Uwe Koch. From 2027 onwards, the Hub in Potsdam will prioritise climate-resilient cultural heritage management, civic engagement and, above all, capacity-building for young people.

The new Hub brings together Potsdam’s local expertise and Europa Nostra’s transnational network. The Palaces and Parks of Potsdam, which are inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List, and the city itself serve as a real-world laboratory for the conservation of cultural landscapes in the context of climate change. To this end, close collaboration with local institutions, such as the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) and the Research Centre Sanssouci (RECS), is foreseen.

title: 2026 Autumn Newsletter: Message by the Executive President and the Secretary General
content:
As an introduction to the Europa Nostra Newsletter issued on 23 October 2026

Dear members, partners and supporters of Europa Nostra,
Dear colleagues and friends,

Welcome to the Autumn edition of the Europa Nostra Newsletter! As you will read, the last  months have been marked by important advocacy action and impactful events held all over Europe, including numerous activities organised as part of our EU-funded European Heritage Hub project which are shared with you through dedicated newsletters.  

A protest gathering will be held on 29 October (09:30-11:30) at Schuman Square in Brussels to Stand up for AgoraEU. © Culture Action Europe
